instructions: Cut the 1 1/4 lb chicken into 1 1/2 inch pieces and pat them dry with paper towels. Squeeze 1 tbsp of juice from half the lemon. In a bowl, toss the chicken with the lemon juice, the 1/4 tsp black pepper, the 1/4 tsp chili powder and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Leave it on the counter while you make the spinach.
Heat 1 tsp of the oil in a large frying pan over high. Add the 1/4 cup cashews and stir for about 1 minute, until they're lightly golden.

Turn the heat to medium and add the spinach a few handfuls at a time, stirring each lot until it collapses before you add the next. Cook for about 6 minutes in all, until it's completely wilted. Take the pan off the heat and let it cool for 5 minutes.
While the spinach cools, finely chop the onion. Seed and finely chop the 2 tomatoes. Peel and grate the ginger, and mince the 4 garlic cloves.
Transfer the spinach and cashews into a blender with 1/2 cup cold water and blend until smooth. Wipe out the pan.

Heat the rest of the oil in the same pan over medium. Add the bay leaf, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, 3 cardamom pods, 3 cloves and the cinnamon stick. After about 20 seconds the cumin will sizzle and smell toasty.
Add the onion and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's light brown and very soft. Don't rush the onion. That's where the flavor starts.
Add the ginger and garlic and cook for 1 minute, until they smell fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and 3/4 tsp of the salt. Cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the tomatoes have broken down and lost their raw smell.

Turn the heat up to medium high and add the chicken. Spread it out and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's pale all over with a few golden spots. Stir in the 3/4 tsp garam masala and cook for 30 seconds.

Pour in 1/2 cup hot water and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom. Cover, turn the heat to medium and cook for 10 to 12 minutes. You're cooking it to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check a thick piece. No thermometer? Cut into the biggest piece: it's done when there's no pink left.
Stir in the spinach puree. If it's as thick as paste, add a splash of hot water. Simmer it uncovered for 3 to 4 minutes, until it's bubbling all over.
Crush the 1 tbsp kasuri methi between your palms into the pan and stir it in. Take the pan off the heat and fish out the bay leaf and the cinnamon stick.
Taste it. If it's flat, add the last 1/4 tsp salt, or a squeeze of the other lemon half.
Drizzle the 2 tbsp cream over the top. Slice the green chili into a small bowl for the table. Serve with basmati rice or naan, with the green chili on the side.
method_notes: All three bloom cumin in fat, cook onion, ginger and garlic with tomato into a base, cook the chicken in it and finish with spinach, kasuri methi and a little cream. Swasthi's Recipes marinates the chicken briefly in lemon, pepper and chili, wilts the spinach with cashews and green chilies and blends it to a smooth puree that goes in at the end; Ministry of Curry blanches and blends the spinach, and Tea for Turmeric chops it and simmers bone-in chicken with it for 35 to 40 minutes. This follows Swasthi's Recipes with thighs instead of breast, and the green chili moved out of the puree and onto the table.
